anti_overlap: Talmud focuses on preserving distinct interpretive voices and layered authority; differs from cathedral which examines build-sequence handoff
Talmud examines whether commentary remains attached to source; differs from heraldry which examines whether identity-specification is compressible into transmissible grammar
Talmud cares about non-flattening of accreted layers; differs from glacier which examines selective forgetting of older strata
decision_lens: Does the brainstorm preserve the interpretive layering — Banks' source novels, shadow-work's hand-rolled implementation, Palettice's abstractions, the Culture-game's future demands — as distinct voices, or does it collapse them into a single synthesised reading that loses the ability to disagree with itself?
distance_rationale: A literary canon that has successfully accreted centuries of interpretation without losing its source text offers a non-software model for how the Culture-as-aggregation-Soul problem might preserve layered meaning rather than collapsing into opaque emergent state.
expected_isomorphisms: Talmud solved the problem of letting a fixed source text accumulate disagreement-preserving commentary through page-layout conventions that keep each voice's authority and chain-of-transmission visible. The Culture-as-Soul aggregation problem is isomorphic — the civ-Soul's facets must aggregate from citizens without losing which citizens, which scars, and which historical interpretations produced the aggregate, or the player loses the ability to read the civilisation's character.
focus: Whether the Culture-as-Soul aggregation problem and the shadow-work-as-reference commitment preserve interpretive layers without flattening them into a single voice
name: fd-talmud-accreted-commentary-canon
persona: Apply the perspective of the Talmudic commentary tradition — they care about whether a canonical source text can accumulate centuries of competing interpretation without losing the source, whether each commentator's voice remains distinguishable from the others, and whether the page layout itself (mishna, gemara, Rashi, Tosafot) encodes which layer is speaking and on whose authority.
review_areas: Whether shadow-work's 31 facets are preserved as an authoritative reference layer or implicitly absorbed and renamed (losing the original commentary)

Whether the Culture-as-aggregation-Soul problem can be implemented as a layered commentary (citizen-Soul facets, civ-Soul projections, collective-memory scars) where each layer remains readable rather than collapsed into an opaque aggregate
Whether the 'thin fiction' naming convention (Idirans, Affront → renamed) preserves the original-text mapping legibly or risks losing the canonical reference once renamed
Whether ship-name LLM derivations encode the chain of authority (which facet, which scar, which archetype contributed) or produce a sealed output with no traceback
Whether deferred Open Questions are recorded as ongoing disputes between named positions (A/B/C with their advocates) or flattened into a single recommendation that hides the disagreement
Whether the brainstorm itself, as a document, is structured so later commentary can attach to specific passages rather than requiring full rewrites

severity_examples.condition: The Culture-as-Soul design (§Open Question 3) is implemented such that the civ-Soul's facet values cannot be traced back to which member-Soul contributions and which historical scars produced them, losing the interpretive layering that makes the civ-Soul legible to the player
severity_examples.scenario: Aggregation Soul collapses to opaque average

severity_examples.condition: After Palettice Phase 2 absorbs shadow-work's AgentPersonality, the original 31-facet justifications and calibration history are not preserved as a referenceable layer, so future decisions to change a facet cannot consult the original commentary on why it was added
severity_examples.scenario: Shadow-work reference loses authority once absorbed

severity_examples.condition: The 'Recommendation (not committed): B + C combined now, A later' style flattens the A/B/C debate into a forward-leaning consensus that loses the dissenting voices' reasons, making it harder to reopen the question when new information arrives
severity_examples.scenario: Open Questions collapse to single recommendation

success_hints: Look for places where multiple authorities (Banks, shadow-work, Palettice, future Culture-game) need to remain distinguishable rather than synthesised
Ask whether aggregation operations preserve the contributing voices or collapse them
Check whether deferred questions retain their dissent or harden prematurely into recommendations
Distinguish canonical source-text commitments from interpretive layers that may be revised
task_context: The brainstorm fuses Banks' Culture novels (canonical fiction), shadow-work's working implementation (operational reference), Palettice's clean abstractions (formal spec), and a speculative Culture-game endpoint (future consumer). Reviewing whether these distinct interpretive layers stay distinguishable or whether the document's drive toward 'one engine' flattens them into a single voice that loses the ability to consult its sources.
